title: Lumina - co-sell pipeline & playbook handoff
summary: Kickoff handoff between Redwood AE/SE and Lumina partnerships/sales to align on co-sell motions, account mapping, a small pilot scope, and security questions. Agreed to run a 6-week pilot (Lumina internal RAG + Redwood hosted inference), Redwood to share playbook and pricing, Lumina to provide sample data and SSO contacts.
next_steps: Jared to send co-sell playbook draft and partner-deck by 2026-03-20
Anu to share anonymized sample dataset and expected throughput by 2026-03-22
Maya to schedule 90-minute technical bench on 2026-03-26 and invite Lumina infra team
Priya to open a shared tracker and add initial account mapping (due 2026-03-24)
action_items: Jared: Draft co-sell contract points + referral credit outline by 2026-03-20
Maya: Run latency + cost bench on Lumina sample and share results by 2026-03-30
Anu: Provide data schema and S3 link (anonymized) by 2026-03-22
Rita: Introduce Lumina legal/security contact (SOC2) by 2026-03-23
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18 15:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Partner Ops), Rita (Lumina Head Partnerships), Ben (Lumina VP Sales), Anu (Lumina Solutions Architect), Marco (Lumina CS)

Summary & topics briefly covered, then transcript below. Note: auto-transcription has occasional mis-words (sock-two for SOC2 etc).

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick round-robin, and then I want to walk through the co-sell playbook and get to the pilot ask.
[00:22] Rita: Hi all, excited to align. We've got a quota motion this quarter that could accelerate if the partnership is tight.
[00:31] Ben: Yeah quick for context, we typically need a pilot to show lift to our sales org — usually a 6 week POC.
[00:45] Maya: Great, and on the Redwood side I'll be leading the technical bench, so we'll validate latency, cost and answer infra questions.
[00:56] Anu: Quick question before you go deep — we have a hybrid infra requirement for specific PHI routes, could that be kept private?
[01:08] Jared: Yes, that's what Redwood Private is for — but for initial pilot we often do Redwood hosted with strict data handling, or a dedicated pool. We'll map options.
[01:22] Rita: Can you remind us differences? We get a bit confused between dedicated, private, and hosted offerings.
[01:30] Maya: Sure — hosted is fastest, dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with isolation so higher SLA, private is V-P-C or on-prem with customer control over VPC and KMS. Sometimes the transcript spells that V-P-C, sorry.
[01:46] Marco: Are there known perf deltas between hosted and dedicated?
[01:52] Maya: Usually dedicated gives tighter latency tail because of no noisy neighbors; but with autoscaling and batching policies you can tune hosted to be very close. We'll show spreadsheet numbers.
[02:10] Ben: On procurement side, what are the typical terms for pilot? Are you doing time-limited credits, reduced rates?
[02:20] Jared: We usually do a pilot credit + pilot pricing. We'll propose a credit and a pilot SOW for 6 weeks; if it hits success criteria — which we should define — we convert to a reserved commit or hosted usage.
[02:36] Rita: Success criteria — we need <150ms median latency for lookup routes and under $0.02 per 1k tokens equivalent ev cost.
[02:48] Maya: Noted, we'll test median and p95. Also need to confirm token accounting for embedding vs generation workflows.
[03:05] Anu: Also for security, Lumina is SOC2 in flight — we need audit log capability, SSO (SAML) and KMS integration for keys.
[03:20] Priya: Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC and K-M-S integrations, and we can surface audit logs in the console. I'll attach the security pack.
[03:35] Ben: Any competitor risks if we move fast? We're evaluating CloudAI and VertexServe as well.
[03:44] Jared: Right, we've seen both. CloudAI is simpler but less optimized for high throughput cost; VertexServe is stronger on on-prem but heavier to adopt. Our playbook highlights win themes.
[04:05] Rita: Let's walk the playbook then — what does co-sell look like from your side?
[04:12] Jared: We propose a three-phase motion: 1) Pilot (6 weeks) — technical bench + value capture, 2) GTM readiness — deck, case study, sales enablement, 3) Rollout — dedicated or hosted commitment and joint exec briefings. We also outline revenue sharing / referral credits.
[04:36] Marco: For GTM materials, do you handle sales decks or do we co-brand?
[04:40] Priya: Co-branding is standard; Redwood supplies a partner deck, case study template, and joint pitch scripts. We'll share a Google Drive link.
[04:54] Anu: On the pilot tech stack — we want to run a RAG flow for internal KB answers plus a rerank route for search. Are there any model constraints?
[05:06] Maya: We have a model catalog; for RAG we recommend a smaller open model for generation + a higher-quality one for rerank, or a single large model depending on latency tradeoffs. We'll recommend quantization profiles.
[05:25] Ben: Can you do a quick ballpark on cost vs latency for a small RAG pilot?
[05:32] Maya: Ballpark: hosted with batching, expect median latency around 180-250ms for single-step generation on our curated model at 1k tokens, cost maybe $0.01–0.03 per 1k tokens depending on batch and caching. Dedicated might shave 30–50ms. These are approximate, we'll bench.
[06:05] Jared: I'll include a mapping table in the deck that compares latency/cost across hosted/dedicated/private, with suggested defaults for pilot.
[06:20] Rita: From Lumina's side, our priority is HIPAA-ish handling and data residency for EU customers — can Redwood host EU-only?
[06:31] Jared: Yes, we have region routing and can pin to EU-hosted instances for data residency. We'll also include contract language for that.
[06:42] Anu: For PKI and keys, we want KMS/HSM — is there a supported integration?
[06:49] Maya: Yes K-M-S integrations are supported, though on private installs HSM options increase. We'll share architecture notes.
[07:05] Ben: Who owns the demo assets? We want a scripted demo for our AE team.
[07:12] Priya: Redwood provides a demo playbook and sample notebook. We'll co-create a 5-10 slide script for Lumina reps.
[07:25] Rita: Ok next — account mapping. We identified 12 target accounts in Q3 where Lumina is active. Can Redwood help prioritize which ones to joint-sell?
[07:36] Jared: Yes, we'll run a win-propensity scoring with your criteria — vertical, tech stack fit, existing Redwood appetite — and then produce a priority heatmap. We'll add it to the shared tracker.
[07:52] Marco: For the pilot we'll need some instrumentation — tracing and token cost visibility. Is that accessible to Lumina?
[07:59] Maya: Yes we can give you console access scoped by RBAC to see token-level metrics, traces and per-route latency. We'll show you a demo on the bench.
[08:15] Anu: On compliance docs — please send SOC2, penetration test summary, and data handling docs.
[08:22] Priya: Will do. I'll attach the security pack and a short FAQ which covers common SOC2/KMS questions.
[08:34] Ben: Who signs the pilot SOW from Redwood?
[08:37] Jared: Typically Redwood legal signs the SOW; we'll share a template so your legal can review early to avoid delays.
[08:47] Rita: Timeline check — if we start week of 3/23 is that feasible?
[08:52] Maya: Tight but doable. We need sample data to run benches, and the Lumina infra team on the 3/26 bench.
[09:03] Anu: We'll try to deliver sample data by 3/22.
[09:07] Jared: Great. Quick technical deep dive — Maya will explain bench design.
[09:12] Maya: Bench plan: ingest anonymized KB into vector DB (we can support open-vector DBs), then run RAG queries at our target QPS, measure median/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll replay real query profiles if you provide them.
[09:37] Ben: Will the bench simulate user concurrency?
[09:40] Maya: Yes concurrency profile will be simulated; we care about prefix KV cache hit rates, batch formation and tail latency.
[09:50] Marco: Any red flags from your initial review of our integration doc?
[09:55] Maya: Minor: a couple of endpoints expect synchronous large payloads — we'll recommend streaming where possible and adjust batch sizing. Also confirm your max sequence lengths.
[10:12] Anu: For regional compliance, our EU accounts require data not leaving EU. Is a private deployment necessary?
[10:18] Jared: For long-term yes, but for pilot you can do EU-hosted region with encryption and contract terms. Private is for permanent host/air-gapped scenarios.
[10:30] Rita: On commercial motion — how are referral credits structured?
[10:34] Jared: Typically a percentage of ARR or a fixed rebate for new net revenue. We'll propose two options in the playbook.
[10:43] Ben: Then final part — success criteria recap.
[10:47] Rita: 1) LIFT: measurable uplift in retrieval accuracy (target +15% to current baseline), 2) Latency p50 < 150ms for routing lookups, 3) Security signoff, 4) Joint-ready case study by end of pilot.
[11:04] Jared: We'll map metrics to experiments and produce an evaluation rubric.
[11:12] Priya: I'll create a shared tracker with owners and dates.
[11:18] Anu: Quick note — our infra team prefers not to share PHI in the pilot; we'll anonymize and apply synthetic identifiers.
[11:25] Maya: That's fine; that still lets us validate latency and token costs.
[11:33] Ben: Anything else on blockers?
[11:35] Rita: Legal review timeline might be the slowest piece.
[11:39] Jared: We'll surface SOW early and propose a standard helper clause for data residency.
[11:46] Marco: Can Redwood also help with a co-sell win narrative for the Lumina reps?
[11:50] Priya: Yes we have a short win matrix we'll adapt.
[11:56] Anu: For the bench on 3/26, who should we expect?
[11:59] Maya: Myself, plus a bench engineer and a solutions architect. We'll share calendar invite.
[12:07] Jared: Ok let's call out explicit owners: Jared sends playbook and commercial options; Maya runs bench; Anu provides data; Priya sets tracker.
[12:18] Rita: Sounds good. End with recap and next steps.
[12:22] Jared: Recap: Playbook and deck by 3/20, sample data by 3/22, tech bench 3/26, shared tracker 3/24. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the security pack.
[12:40] Ben: Thanks everyone.
[12:44] Jared: Thanks — meeting adjourned.

Notes: references to docs: playbook doc: https://drive.google.com/lumina-playbook (placeholder), bench spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/lumina-bench (placeholder).
